# Reliable End-to-End Text-to-SQL Generation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#rts-plus)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://openproceedings.org/2026/conf/edbt/paper-177.pdf) · EDBT 2026 short paper, printed pages 544–550

**Reading coverage:** All seven PDF pages, sections 1–7, equations 1–3 and conformal-set construction, tables 1–2, figures/captions and references; no supplement in the supplied paper.

## Research question

Schema linking can be correct while the final generated SQL is wrong; the pipeline needs a way to defer uncertain outputs.

## Method

RTS++ uses RTS schema linking, multiple SQL candidates, decoding probabilities, execution-result clusters, entropy and reranker scores. A calibration quantile forms a candidate set; empty or ambiguous sets trigger abstention or user selection.

## Evaluation

Spider test and BIRD development results compare reranking, abstention and feedback variants. Calibration uses training data; error tolerance is 0.1 and feedback is assumed accurate. Reported execution accuracy is selective accuracy on the non-abstained subset, accompanied by abstention rates.

## What the results support

Reported accuracy rises when low-confidence cases are withheld, with additional gains under ideal feedback. The headline 92.3%/92.5% values are not full-coverage autonomous accuracy. Removing execution entropy lowers reported reliability and abstention.

## Limits and qualifications

The stated conformal coverage target is not a demonstrated conditional semantic-error guarantee for all executed requests. Candidate completeness and detailed calibration assumptions are not resolved by the short paper. Result normalization ignores some ordering distinctions; warehouse cost and safe execution require separate treatment.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful selective-generation architecture, provided coverage, ideal feedback and database-relative correctness remain explicit.
